backlog.spec: Provide jac for the objective (-1 on radii, 0 on centres) and an analytic Jacobian for the constraint function (pairwise distance, wall and positivity rows) via the constraints dict 'jac'. This removes finite-difference cost (about 96 evaluations per gradient) and allows many more restarts and iterations in the same CPU time.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Set MAX_ITER=500 so that SLSQP converges fully in each run instead of stopping at 200 iterations. Best combined with an analytic Jacobian.
backlog.title: Increase MAX_ITER to 500

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9 to use more of the 30 s budget. The final run may overshoot a little, so keep the margin well under 45 s.
backlog.title: Use TIME_FRACTION 0.9

backlog.spec: Initialise centres on a jittered 6x6 grid with 32 of the 36 cells chosen at random, plus noise of 0.03. Use this instead of uniform random starts, so that the starts are better spread.
backlog.title: Grid-perturbed initialisation

backlog.spec: After a few random restarts, spend the remaining time perturbing the best solution (Gaussian noise sd 0.02-0.05 on centres, radii scaled by 0.8) and re-running SLSQP. Keep the result if the sum of radii improves.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the best packing

backlog.spec: Perturbation move on the incumbent: take the smallest 1-2 circles and move them to random positions (or to the largest hole found by sampling points), set their radii small, then re-run SLSQP. Accept if better.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circle move

backlog.spec: Stage 1: run a short SLSQP (maxiter 60) on many random starts. Stage 2: run a full SLSQP (maxiter 400) on only the top 20% of the stage 1 results.
backlog.title: Two-stage optimisation

backlog.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS to 0.02 so that the initial point is feasible and the optimiser grows the radii gradually. Check whether the results improve.
backlog.title: Smaller initial radius

backlog.spec: Draw the initial radii from uniform(0.03, 0.12) per circle instead of a constant, to make the size distribution more varied.
backlog.title: Initial radius random per circle

backlog.spec: Replace _repair with a fixed-centre LP (scipy linprog) maximising the sum of radii subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distance, r>=0. Then subtract 1e-12 relative slack. This recovers the exact optimal radii for the given centres.
backlog.title: Better repair via LP

backlog.spec: Polish the best packing with alternating steps: an LP for the radii at fixed centres, then SLSQP from this point with a tight ftol (1e-15). Finish with a repair step.
backlog.title: Final polish with LP

backlog.spec: In the later polishing runs, include only the pairs with distance less than r_i+r_j+0.15. This shrinks the constraint set from 496 to about 120, which makes SLSQP much faster. Check validity afterwards with a full repair.
backlog.title: Sparse near-neighbour constraints

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a few hundred steps of L-BFGS-B on the penalty energy -sum r + mu*sum(overlap^2) with mu increasing. Use the result to start SLSQP from a nearly feasible state.
backlog.title: Penalty-based pre-optimiser

backlog.spec: Start from a hex-like lattice with row counts such as 6,5,6,5,6,4 (adjusted to 32), with random jitter and a random rotation of the row structure. Use the radii of about 0.08.
backlog.title: Hex-lattice initialisation

backlog.spec: Alternate between uniform random, jittered grid and hex starts for the restarts, to diversify the basins.
backlog.title: Mixed-init restarts

backlog.spec: Generate 16 random circles and mirror them across a random axis (x->1-x) to get 32 circles with mirror symmetry, then run the full unconstrained SLSQP. Some good packings are close to symmetric.
backlog.title: Symmetry-exploiting starts

backlog.spec: Use ftol=1e-6 in the screening runs and discard the starts whose sum of radii after 50 iterations is below the running median. Continue only the promising ones.
backlog.title: Cap SLSQP ftol looser for screening

backlog.spec: For the polishing of the best 3 candidates, run scipy trust-constr with analytic gradients, then repair. Check that it escapes the SLSQP stalls.
backlog.title: Use trust-constr alternative

backlog.spec: Write the pair constraints as d^2-(ri+rj)^2>=0, with ri+rj>=0 enforced via the r>=0 bounds. This is smoother and has no sqrt singularity. Provide the analytic Jacobian. Use bounds for r and c instead of the wall constraints.
backlog.title: Vectorised constraint with squared distances

backlog.spec: Pass bounds (0,1) for centres and (0,0.5) for radii to SLSQP and keep only the pair constraints and the wall constraints. Reducing the inequality count helps speed.
backlog.title: Use bounds instead of wall constraints

backlog.spec: Compute iu once at module level per n and cache it. Avoid reallocating it in each call, with small speedups of the constraint evaluation.
backlog.title: Precompute index arrays

backlog.spec: After the perturbation, multiply the radii by 0.9 before the next SLSQP run so the start is feasible and SLSQP works from the interior.
backlog.title: Radius shrink before final SLSQP

backlog.spec: Perturbation move: choose a large and a small circle in the incumbent and swap their radii (keeping the centres), then run SLSQP. Accept if better.
backlog.title: Perturb by swapping a big and small circle

backlog.spec: Keep the top 5 distinct packings. In each iteration, pick one at random, perturb it with a random move (noise, relocate, swap) and re-optimise. Replace the worst if better.
backlog.title: Population with elitism

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, decrease the perturbation sd linearly from 0.06 to 0.005 over the time budget, which moves from global to local search.
backlog.title: Annealed perturbation scale

backlog.spec: Set SHRINK to 1e-11 and verify with an exact pairwise check, shrinking only the offending radii. This loses less radius than the 1e-9 shrink and still passes the 1e-10 tolerance.
backlog.title: Safer shrink and tighter validity

backlog.spec: Estimate the time of one run and stop launching new runs when the remaining time is less than 1.5x this estimate, which allows TIME_FRACTION 0.95 without a risk of overshoot.
backlog.title: Time check inside restarts

backlog.spec: Start with fixed equal radii packing: maximise the common radius with SLSQP (a cheap problem), then release the radii to be free and optimise the sum. This gives a well-spread start.
backlog.title: Fewer-dimension relaxed start

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run 20 iterations of repulsion (move each centre away from its neighbours with a force 1/d^2, clipped to the square) from the random start. This gives well-separated starts.
backlog.title: Lloyd-style spreading of initial centres

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, replace uniform random centres with a hex-like lattice: choose rows of alternating 6 and 5 circles (6 rows gives 33 points; drop one random point to get 32), spacing to fill the unit square, plus Gaussian jitter sd 0.02 and a random choice of row count/orientation (swap x and y with prob 0.5). Keep the common-radius pre-stage and the SLSQP step unchanged. Use this for half of the restarts and random uniform for the rest.
backlog.title: Hex-lattice jittered starts

backlog.spec: Remove the four wall constraint blocks from the constraint function in the main SLSQP and pass bounds instead: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Add the wall constraints back only as linear inequalities c-r>=0 and 1-c-r>=0 via a LinearConstraint-free approach: keep them, but also pass bounds so that SLSQP handles box constraints natively. The aim is a smaller, better-conditioned constraint set. The repair step stays.
backlog.title: Bounds for walls instead of constraints

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, with probability 0.5 pick one of the 8 largest and one of the 8 smallest circles of the best packing, swap their centre positions (radii stay attached to the circles' original slots, so the big circle lands in the small one's place), add jitter sd 0.01, then run SLSQP. Otherwise do the existing Gaussian perturbation. Accept if the repaired sum improves.
backlog.title: Swap big/small circle radii move

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, make the Gaussian jitter sd decay linearly from 0.05 at the switch time to 0.005 at the end of the time budget, instead of a fixed 0.02. Larger early moves explore, smaller late moves refine.
backlog.title: Annealed perturbation scale

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP on fresh starts, run L-BFGS-B on variables (centres, radii) minimizing -sum(r) + mu * (sum of squared pair overlaps + squared wall violations) with analytic gradient via numpy vectorisation, with mu increasing 10, 100, 1000 over three short runs (maxiter 100 each). Feed the result into the SLSQP. This replaces the common-radius SLSQP stage which is slower per start.
backlog.title: Penalty-based pre-optimiser with L-BFGS

backlog.spec: For each fresh start, run SLSQP with maxiter 40 and ftol 1e-5. Only if the resulting repaired sum is within 0.01 of the best so far, continue with a second SLSQP from that point with maxiter 200 and ftol 1e-9. This saves time on poor basins and permits more starts in the exploration phase.
backlog.title: Looser-ftol screening then full refine

backlog.spec: Initialise radii in the main SLSQP start as random uniform in [0.03, 0.12] per circle rather than a common radius, after the common-radius stage, so that the optimiser begins with a mix of big and small circles, which the best known packings have. Centres are kept from the pre-stage but 30 percent of circles are re-drawn at random positions.
backlog.title: Per-circle random initial radii

backlog.spec: Draw 32 uniform random points, then run 5 Lloyd iterations: sample 4000 random points in the square, assign each to the nearest centre, move each centre to the mean of its cell. Use the result as initial centres. This gives evenly spread starts before the common-radius stage. Use it for 50 percent of restarts.
backlog.title: Lloyd-spread initial centres

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, with probability 0.5: remove the 2 smallest-radius circles of the best packing, then find the largest empty spots by sampling 20000 random points and picking those with maximum distance to the surfaces of the remaining circles and walls (greedy, 2 spots well separated), place the removed circles there with radius 0.02, and run SLSQP. Otherwise do the existing perturbation.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert into largest hole

backlog.spec: After the time loop, fix the best centres and solve an LP with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) maximizing sum of radii subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij-1e-12, r_i<=wall distance-1e-12, r>=0. Then use it only if the exact validity check passes and the sum exceeds the current. Reserve 0.5 s for this by lowering TIME_FRACTION to 0.78. This replaces the heuristic repair gain of shrink 1e-9.
backlog.title: Final LP radius re-optimisation with active-set polish

backlog.spec: Change the basin-hopping switch time in solve from 0.4*time_limit to 0.25*time_limit so more of the budget is spent perturbing the best packing. Keep everything else the same.
backlog.title: Replicate-friendly switch fraction 0.25

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, with probability 0.3 build the start by taking the best packing and swapping the positions (centres) of two circles with clearly different radii (pick one from the top third by radius and one from the bottom third), keeping radii unchanged as initial values, then add small Gaussian jitter (sd 0.01) and run the SLSQP polish. Otherwise use the existing jitter perturbation.
backlog.title: Swap big/small circle radii move

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, run the main SLSQP with maxiter 60 first. Only if the resulting sum of radii is within 0.02 of the best-so-far sum, continue SLSQP from that result with maxiter 200 to converge. Otherwise discard. This saves time on poor basins and allows more restarts.
backlog.title: Loose-ftol screening then refine

backlog.spec: Set MAX_ITER to 400 only for the basin-hopping phase calls (start is not None), leaving fresh starts at 200, so late refinements converge fully.
backlog.title: Larger MAX_ITER with basin-hopping only

backlog.spec: Replace always-perturb-the-best with a Metropolis chain: keep a current packing; perturb it, polish, accept if sum improves or with probability exp((new-cur)/0.003); track the global best separately. Reset current to best every 15 steps.
backlog.title: Accept-based basin hopping chain

backlog.spec: Before the full SLSQP on fresh starts, add a short stage with objective -sum(r) + 0.5*sum(r**2)*... no: use objective -sum(r) plus a penalty 0.2*var(r) for maxiter 30, then drop the penalty and run the normal objective. This regularises toward equal radii early and avoids degenerate tiny circles.
backlog.title: Symmetric-pair radius smoothing regularizer start

backlog.spec: Keep MAX_ITER=200 for fresh starts but pass maxiter=400 to _solve_once when start is not None (basin-hopping phase), so perturbed packings converge fully to the local optimum. Implement by adding a maxiter parameter to _solve_once defaulting to MAX_ITER and setting it to 400 when start is given.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent with MAX_ITER 400 in basin-hopping only

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase keep a current packing (initially best). Each iteration perturbs the current one with Gaussian sd 0.03, re-optimises, repairs, and accepts it as current if its sum is within 0.003 of the current sum (Metropolis-like with temperature 0.002: accept with prob exp((new-cur)/0.002)). Track the global best separately and return it. Reset current to best every 15 iterations.
backlog.title: Accept-based basin-hopping chain

backlog.spec: Remove the 4n wall constraints and the r>=0 constraints in the main SLSQP, and pass bounds instead: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Instead enforce the walls by reparametrising: keep wall inequality constraints only for circles but not... Simpler: keep the wall constraints but add bounds to the variables (centres [0,1], radii [0,0.5]) to reduce wasted steps, and drop the separate r constraint rows. Verify the final repair still ensures validity.
backlog.title: Bounds for wall constraints

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, sample initial per-circle radii for the common-radius stage output as a mix: after the common-radius SLSQP, set radii to 0.8*r for 20 randomly chosen circles and 1.2*r for the other 12 (r the common radius), giving a size-diverse start. Then run the main SLSQP. This differs from per-circle uniform radii which failed; it uses a bimodal structure similar to good known packings.
backlog.title: Sorted-radii big-small structured start

backlog.spec: Run fresh restarts for 50% of the time, keeping the best 3 results. For the remaining time cycle through the 3 elites round-robin as basin-hopping seeds with jitter sd 0.02, replacing an elite only when a child beats it. Return the best overall.
backlog.title: Two-level time split with elite pool restart

backlog.spec: After the final best packing is chosen, fix centres and solve a scipy linprog maximising sum radii subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij-2e-12 and wall constraints r_i<=min wall distance - 1e-12, r>=0. Return LP radii if the exact double-precision validity check (pairwise and walls with tolerance 1e-10) passes; otherwise fall back to the old repair. This recovers the 1e-9 shrink loss per circle (~3e-8 total) and any slack.
backlog.title: Soft tolerance repair via exact LP then tiny shrink

backlog.spec: In the common-radius stage nothing differentiates circles, so add to the main SLSQP's first 60 iterations a nothing-changing objective: run main SLSQP in two passes, first maximising sum(r) - 0.05*sum((r-mean(r))**2) with maxiter 60, then the true objective sum(r) from that result with maxiter 200. The first pass discourages degenerate tiny circles early, giving better basins.
backlog.title: Penalty on small radii (size-spread regulariser) in early stage

backlog.spec: Generate 12 fresh starts at a time through the common-radius stage only (cheap), compute a quick score for each as the sum of radii after a 30-iteration main SLSQP, then fully refine only the best 2 with the full MAX_ITER. Repeat this batch cycle until 40% of the time is used, then proceed to basin hopping as before.
backlog.title: Batch of cheap starts, top-k refinement

backlog.spec: In _solve_once main SLSQP call, remove the four wall constraint blocks (c-r, 1-c-r) from cons and instead keep only pair constraints plus r>=0. Pass bounds to minimize: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Then, after solving, _repair already clips radii to wall distance. This shrinks the constraint count from ~496+160 to ~496 and speeds up each SLSQP iteration, permitting more restarts in the same time. Note: wall feasibility is not enforced by bounds alone (r<=c), so keep it simple: add bounds c in [0.01,0.99], r in [0.01,0.5] and keep wall constraints only for the radius-vs-centre relation if results look invalid.
backlog.title: Wall bounds instead of wall constraints

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, with probability 0.5 build the perturbed start by taking the best packing, removing the smallest 1-3 circles, and placing each at the point (from 2000 random candidates in the square) maximising the minimum of distance to other circles' surfaces (distance to centre minus radius) and wall distance, giving it a radius equal to that clearance (min 0.01). Then run the normal SLSQP polish from this start (with the neighbour-pruned constraints) and accept if the repaired sum improves. Otherwise use the existing Gaussian jitter.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert into largest hole

backlog.spec: Keep MAX_ITER=200 for fresh starts but pass maxiter=500 and ftol=1e-10 to SLSQP when start is not None (the basin-hopping phase), so that perturbed local refinements converge fully to tight local optima. Implement by adding a maxiter parameter to _solve_once.
backlog.title: Higher MAX_ITER in basin-hopping only

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, replace uniform random centres by 32 random points relaxed with 5 Lloyd iterations: sample 4000 uniform points, assign each to nearest centre, move each centre to the mean of its assigned points (keep if empty). This gives a blue-noise centre set. Then proceed with the existing common-radius SLSQP and main SLSQP.
backlog.title: Lloyd-relaxed initial centres

backlog.spec: After the common-radius stage, set initial per-circle radii by a structured two-size pattern: the circles with the 8 largest distances to their nearest neighbours get radius 1.4*r_common and the rest get 0.9*r_common (clipped to wall distance). Use these as x0 radii for the main SLSQP. Optimal packings for this problem have mixed sizes, so this seeds the size heterogeneity.
backlog.title: Radius-spread starting radii from sorted sizes

backlog.spec: For the first 40% of the time: run many fresh starts with SLSQP maxiter 40 only, storing (sum of radii, raw x). Then take the top 8 by raw radii sum (after _repair) and continue each with SLSQP maxiter 300 from its stored state. Keep the best, then enter the existing basin-hopping phase for the remaining time.
backlog.title: Batch of cheap starts then top-k refinement

backlog.spec: In the main SLSQP for fresh starts, use objective -sum(r) + 0.5*sum((r - mean(r))**2)*... no: instead use objective -sum(r) - 0.3*sum(r**2) first for maxiter 40, which favours unequal sizes with large circles, then rerun the normal objective -sum(r) from the result for the remaining iterations. Only the final objective determines acceptance.
backlog.title: Small-radius penalty regulariser early

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, add a move: pick a random circle and translate it and its 3 nearest neighbours by a common random vector of magnitude 0.05-0.1, plus jitter 0.01 on all others; shrink radii of the moved circles by 20%. Then SLSQP polish. This produces collective rearrangements that independent Gaussian jitter cannot.
backlog.title: Perturb by shifting a row of neighbours

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed switch at 0.4*time_limit to basin hopping with: switch when no improvement of the best sum greater than 1e-4 has occurred in the last 6 fresh restarts, or at 0.6*time_limit at the latest. Basin hopping then takes the rest. Tracks restarts since last improvement in solve.
backlog.title: Time-adaptive switch using stagnation

backlog.spec: Reserve the final 8% of the time (TIME_FRACTION stays 0.8 but additionally use leftover 0.1*time_limit): run SLSQP with ftol=1e-13 and maxiter 1000 on the best packing with only near-neighbour (d<0.05) constraints, then repair, and keep it if the sum improves. Avoid anything but one extra call.
backlog.title: Final LP-plus-tight SLSQP polish of top candidates in the last second

backlog.spec: For half of fresh starts after the common-radius stage, set per-circle initial radii to a bimodal pattern: 20 circles at 0.10 and 12 at 0.07 (randomly assigned), scaled so the sum equals the common-radius result times 32. Centres come from the common-radius solution. This mimics the large and small mix found in best known packings.
backlog.title: Sorted-radii structured start

backlog.spec: After the time loop, take the best packing, identify active contacts (pair gap < 1e-7, wall gap < 1e-7), and solve the KKT-style equality system for centres and radii with a few Gauss-Newton steps (np.linalg.lstsq on the active constraint residuals, minimum-norm step) to remove the residual slack. Then run the repair step. Accept only if the sum of radii is higher.
backlog.title: Final active-set LP polish with Newton on contacts

backlog.spec: Keep the basin-hopping phase, but each chain is a Metropolis walk with temperature decaying geometrically from 0.004 to 0.0003 over a chain of 15 steps, jitter sd 0.03. After each chain, reset the current packing to the global best. Track the global best separately so it never worsens.
backlog.title: Annealed Metropolis with restarts from elite

backlog.spec: In the common-radius init stage, replace the objective -r by -r + 0.5*sum((x_i-mean)^2) of centre positions around nothing... Instead use objective -r - 0.02*sum(log(dist to nearest neighbour)) to encourage spread. Use maxiter 30. Then the main SLSQP as before. This regularises only the init and is dropped for the main stage.
backlog.title: Penalised soft-min radius regulariser removal late

backlog.spec: Run the main SLSQP twice per fresh start: first with maxiter 80, then restart from the result with a 0.005 centre jitter limited to circles whose radius is below the median, maxiter 120. Keep the better of the two. The second round lets small circles escape bad pockets without a full basin hop.
backlog.title: Use trust-constr-free SLSQP with warm-started multipliers by two-round solve

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, with probability 0.3, build the start by taking the half of the best packing with x<0.5 (circles by centre), reflecting it across x=0.5 to replace the other half (for n=32 take the 16 closest to the left wall plus their mirrors), add jitter sd 0.01 and run SLSQP. Otherwise do the normal jitter. Keep the result only if better.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric basin-hopping move

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, after the common-radius stage, keep only pairs whose centre distance is below 0.35 in the constraint set (as is done for basin hopping with d0<0.15), then after SLSQP finishes, check all pairs; if any is violated by more than 1e-9, rerun SLSQP with all pairs from that result for maxiter 50. This lowers the per-iteration cost during most of the search.
backlog.title: Adaptive pair-constraint neighbour list

backlog.spec: After each _solve_once, replace radii by the exact LP optimum for the fixed centres: maximize sum r subject to r_i+r_j <= d_ij (only for pairs with d_ij<0.3), r_i <= wall distance, r>=0, using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). Subtract SHRINK afterwards and run the existing _repair for safety. Use these radii for ranking best, so basin-hopping compares true local quality of each centre configuration.
backlog.title: LP-optimal radii after every SLSQP

backlog.spec: At the end (reserve last 1.5 s), take the best packing, identify active contacts (pair gap<1e-6, wall gap<1e-6), and solve the square system of active equalities with scipy.optimize.least_squares (or fsolve-style Newton using lstsq) over centres and radii starting from the current values, accepting the result only if the sum of radii rises and _repair leaves it valid. This pushes the SLSQP result to machine-precision convergence of contacts.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish of the best packing

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, draw per-circle target radii from a bimodal distribution (about 12 big circles of 0.11 and 20 small circles of 0.06), place centres by sequential random dart throwing largest first so no target discs overlap (reduce radii by 0.9 each 200 failed attempts), then run the common-radius stage and the main SLSQP with these radii as the initial radii. Known good packings of this problem have mixed sizes.
backlog.title: Radius-ordered structured start

backlog.spec: In the main SLSQP for fresh starts, run a first stage of 60 iterations with objective -sum(r) + 0.5*sum((r-mean(r))**2) pulling radii toward uniformity to avoid early collapsing of small circles, then a second stage with the true objective from that result (maxiter 200). Only apply to fresh starts, not basin hopping.
backlog.title: Soft-min size-spread regulariser decaying to zero

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, each iteration generates 4 jittered copies of the best packing, runs each for maxiter 30 with sparse neighbour constraints, and then only continues the one with the highest sum of radii (after repair) to maxiter 200. This screens perturbations at about 1/3 the cost per candidate.
backlog.title: Parallel-in-time batch: evaluate several perturbations with cheap SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a final mini-phase using the last 10% of the time: take the best packing, and run SLSQP with ftol=1e-12 and maxiter 500 with sparse pair constraints (centre distance < 0.3), starting from the best without jitter. Accept only if the repaired sum of radii is higher. This extracts the last digits of convergence beyond maxiter 200.
backlog.title: Trust-constr free: SLSQP with squared-radius smoothing of final stage

backlog.spec: For half of fresh starts, generate initial centres by simulating a quick event-free compression: start 32 random points, run 150 steps where each point is pushed away from neighbours with force 1/d^3 (clip step 0.01) and pushed inside the box, with a growing virtual radius used to scale the force range. Then use these centres with the common-radius SLSQP stage. Distinct from the earlier 1/d^2 repulsion test by using growth-scaled range and many more steps.
backlog.title: Compression-based starts (Lubachevsky-like)

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, with probability 0.5 apply jitter only to circles whose centre lies within 0.25 of the square boundary using sd 0.05, and leave interior circles unmoved; otherwise use the existing jitter. Best packings typically have a rigid interior and flexible boundary arrangement.
backlog.title: Boundary-biased circle count perturbation

backlog.spec: Split the time budget into three independent chains: each runs fresh starts for 25% of the budget then basin hops from its own best for 10%. At the end return the best of the three. Differs from the elite pool because chains never share state, which preserves diversity across basins.
backlog.title: Dual-seed time split with independent chains

backlog.spec: Precompute triu indices once per n in a module-level dict, and in the main SLSQP use an analytic Jacobian only for the pair block via scipy sparse-to-dense assembly, built with np.zeros and fancy indexing. Ignore wall rows in the Jacobian by providing bounds instead of wall constraints. Goal is purely speed: more restarts in 24 s.
backlog.title: Cache constraint index arrays and use float32-free vectorised neighbour list

backlog.spec: Change MAX_ITER from 200 to 400 for every SLSQP call, including fresh starts and basin hopping. Keep everything else unchanged. Longer runs may converge more starts to tight local optima. Fewer restarts is the trade-off.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent with MAX_ITER 400 for fresh starts

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, remove the four wall-inequality blocks from cons. Pass bounds to SLSQP instead: centre coordinates in [0.0, 1.0] and radii in [0, 0.5]. Keep the pair constraints and the r>=0 handling. The radius-vs-wall constraints c-r>=0 and 1-c-r>=0 are still needed, so keep them as linear constraints, but drop the redundant r>=0 block, which bounds now cover. This shrinks the constraint vector and speeds up each SLSQP iteration, which allows more restarts.
backlog.title: Wall bounds instead of wall constraints

backlog.spec: After the search, take the best packing. Identify the active contacts: pairs with gap < 1e-7 and wall contacts with slack < 1e-7. Solve the square or least-squares system that sets those gaps to exactly zero with scipy.optimize.least_squares or a few Gauss-Newton steps on (centres, radii). Accept the result only if the sum of radii does not drop after the existing _repair step. This removes SLSQP's residual violation, which _repair would otherwise pay for in shrinkage.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish of the final packing

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, draw target radii from a bimodal mix, with 8 circles near 0.13 and 24 near 0.08. Place centres by Poisson-disc dart throwing, largest first, using those radii. Set the initial radii variables to 0.8 times the targets and skip the common-radius stage. The best known packings have mixed radii, so this starts closer to them. Slot 43 used something similar, so make this one deterministic about the counts and add no jitter beyond the placement.
backlog.title: Size-structured start with big/small mix

backlog.spec: In the fresh-start stage, run a first SLSQP of 40 iterations with objective -sum(r) + lam*sum((r-mean(r))^2) and lam=1.0. Then run the normal -sum(r) objective from the result. The penalty discourages tiny circles early and lets circles grow into holes later.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius regulariser decaying to zero

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, generate 6 jittered copies of the best packing at once. Run SLSQP with maxiter 30 on each. Continue only the one with the best repaired sum of radii to maxiter 200. This gives a cheap best-of-k selection per step, so most of the compute goes to promising moves.
backlog.title: Batch of perturbations screened with short SLSQP

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, compute for each circle of the best packing how many contacts it has (gap < 1e-6, walls included). Choose circles with 2 or fewer contacts, the rattlers, and re-place them at random inside the largest empty region. Pick the region by evaluating 500 random points and taking the one with the largest distance to the nearest circle edge. Then run SLSQP. Circles with few contacts are wasted area.
backlog.title: Contact-graph guided perturbation: free the loosest circles

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, apply a random one of the 8 square symmetries to the best packing before jittering it. Use sd 0.02. SLSQP is not symmetric under the constraint ordering, so reflected starts follow different paths and reach different nearby optima. This is a cheap way to diversify.
backlog.title: Lower-time-fraction basin hopping with restarts from rotated or reflected best

backlog.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS to 0.02 and INIT_LOW to 0.05 for the first SLSQP or common-radius stage. Starting with small circles keeps the early constraints inactive and gives smoother growth. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Smaller initial radius for the common-radius stage

backlog.spec: Reserve the last 10% of the time budget. Spend it running SLSQP with ftol=1e-12 and maxiter 500 on the best packing and on its top two distinct alternatives from earlier. Apply _repair to each result and keep the best. Spend the first 90% as it is now, with TIME_FRACTION 0.8 replaced by the equivalent split. SLSQP's default ftol of 1e-6 may stop short of full convergence.
backlog.title: Time-sliced schedule with a final tight-ftol refinement

backlog.spec: Make no change to train.py except a harmless comment, to get another replicate of the incumbent and estimate its true mean. Many past slots scored exactly -2.9374, so this measures whether that value is a stable optimum or luck.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent unchanged

backlog.spec: In the main SLSQP, drop the four wall inequality blocks and the r>=0 block from cons. Pass bounds to minimize: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Add linear wall constraints only for c-r>=0 and 1-c-r>=0 if needed to stay valid. The aim is a smaller constraint vector (fewer rows, faster QP steps), and so more restarts in the same time. Keep _repair as it is.
backlog.title: Wall bounds instead of wall constraints

backlog.spec: After the search, take the best packing and identify the active contacts (pair gaps < 1e-7 and wall gaps < 1e-7). Solve the KKT-style system by a few Newton iterations on those equalities, with least-squares steps via np.linalg.lstsq, to drive the gaps to exactly 0. Then run _repair. Keep the result only if the sum of radii is higher and the packing is valid. This recovers the 1e-9-scale slack in the shrink step.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish of final packing

backlog.spec: For half of fresh starts, draw initial radii from a bimodal distribution (about 12 large circles of 0.11 and 20 small of 0.07). Place centres by sequential largest-first random rejection sampling so that no circles overlap. Then run the common-radius stage and the main SLSQP from those radii and positions. This seeds the large/small mix that the best known packings have.
backlog.title: Sorted-radii structured start

backlog.spec: In the first SLSQP stage of fresh starts, add the term lam*sum((r-mean(r))**2) to the objective, with lam=0.5 (this favours equal radii and so gives a more spread-out layout). Then re-run SLSQP with lam=0 from that result. This is a different shape of regulariser from the earlier -0.3*sum(r^2) one, which pushes the other way.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius spread regulariser decaying to zero

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, start each attempt from a random one of the 8 symmetries of the square applied to the best packing (centres c -> 1-c and/or swapped x/y), plus a jitter of sd 0.02. This adds variety to the starts while keeping the structure, which differs from the earlier mirror starts (those used half-random circles).
backlog.title: Reflected/rotated best restarts

backlog.spec: In the common-radius stage, set INIT_RADIUS to 0.02 (instead of 0.05) and allow maxiter 80. This starts from a looser state, so the stage ends in different basins.
backlog.title: Smaller common-radius initial radius

backlog.spec: Run fresh restarts in two independent pools, each for 20% of the time, using separate rng streams. Take the better pool's best, then run basin hopping for the rest of the time. Also give the second pool's best a 20% chance of being the basin-hopping start, to diversify.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the best of two independent halves

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, with probability 0.3 start SLSQP from a random one of the 8 square symmetries (reflections/rotations, applied as c -> 1-c and/or axis swap) of the best packing with small jitter (sd 0.01) instead of the plain best. Radii are unchanged. Keep the result only if it beats best. This diversifies the jitter basin without changing the objective.
backlog.title: Reflected/rotated best restarts

backlog.spec: After the main loop (reserve about 0.5 s), take the best packing and identify active constraints (pair gaps and wall gaps below 1e-7). Run a few Newton or Gauss-Newton steps using np.linalg.lstsq on the equality system gap_k(x)=0 for the active set, taking the minimum-norm correction from the current point. Accept the step only if the sum of radii after _repair is higher than before. This removes the residual slack left by SLSQP's ftol.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish of final packing

backlog.spec: Pass options ftol=1e-10 and maxiter=300 to the main SLSQP, and cut fresh starts that have not reached sum of radii above 2.85 after the first 60 iterations. To do this, run in two calls: maxiter 60, check the sum of radii, then continue from the result only if it is promising. Spend the saved time on extra restarts.
backlog.title: Lower SLSQP ftol in main solve with more iterations in fresh starts

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, run the main SLSQP in three stages with objective -sum(r) + lam*sum((r-mean(r))**2) and lam = 0.5, 0.15, 0 at maxiter 40, 40 and 120. The early spread penalty favours uniform sizes, which keeps the optimizer away from degenerate tiny-circle local optima. The final stage uses the true objective.
backlog.title: Soft-min size-spread regulariser decaying to zero

backlog.spec: After each _solve_once, with the centres fixed, solve the radius LP with scipy.optimize.linprog (maximise sum r s.t. r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distances, r>=0, method highs), then apply a tiny shrink of 1e-10 and verify validity. Use the LP radii for comparing candidates and for selecting the best. Compare candidates by this value so that basin-hopping chooses on true quality.
backlog.title: Exact LP radius re-optimisation after each SLSQP

backlog.spec: In fresh starts, after the common-radius stage, build the pair list only from pairs whose centre distance is under 0.35. Rebuild the list once after 60 SLSQP iterations, then run the final SLSQP to completion with the rebuilt list. This cuts constraint count by about 60 percent and gives faster iterations and more restarts. Verify the final validity in _repair with all pairs.
backlog.title: Constraint-count schedule: drop far pairs after warm start

backlog.spec: For half of fresh starts, place about 12 circle centres along the square's boundary at distance 0.08 from the walls, evenly spaced with jitter, and the rest uniformly random in the interior [0.2,0.8]^2. Best known packings tend to have a ring of boundary circles around an irregular interior. Then run the usual common-radius SLSQP and main SLSQP.
backlog.title: Ring-boundary structured starts

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, generate 8 perturbed copies of the best packing (sd uniform in 0.01 to 0.04), run each through SLSQP with maxiter 30, then continue the top 2 to maxiter 200. Different from earlier screening because it screens on the perturbation scale and runs two finalists to convergence.
backlog.title: Batch of perturbed copies, keep best by short run

backlog.spec: For a fresh start, run the first SLSQP stage (maxiter 60) with the objective -sum(w_i r_i), where w_i is uniform in [0.7, 1.3] per circle, drawn from rng. This tilts the landscape toward different size distributions. Then run the true -sum(r) objective from that point with maxiter 200. It diversifies the basins reached.
backlog.title: Randomised radius-weighted objective

backlog.spec: In the late phase, take the best packing and delete a random circle. Re-optimise the remaining 31 with SLSQP (maxiter 100). Then insert a new circle at the largest empty spot, found by sampling 5000 points and picking the one with the biggest distance-to-nearest-circle-surface. Run the full SLSQP on all 32 from there. Accept as best if it improves.
backlog.title: Remove one circle, solve 31, re-add with LP

backlog.spec: After the search, take the best packing and identify active constraints (pair gaps and wall gaps below 1e-7). Solve the KKT-like system with np.linalg.lstsq for a Newton step on centres and radii to push active constraints to exactly 0 gap. Do this for at most 5 iterations. Accept the result only if _repair gives a larger radius sum than before. Do not change anything else.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish of final packing

backlog.spec: In the cheap common-radius SLSQP stage for fresh starts, set the initial common radius to 0.03 instead of INIT_RADIUS 0.05. Keep everything else the same. This tests how sensitive the starting basin is to the initial radius.
backlog.title: Smaller common-radius init

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, add a first SLSQP stage of 40 iterations with objective -sum(r) + lam*sum((r-mean(r))^2) with lam=1.0. Then run the normal objective with lam=0. This favours near-uniform radii early, and the main stage then finds the heterogeneous optimum. Use the same constraints.
backlog.title: Soft-min spread regulariser decaying to zero

backlog.spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1] and radii in [0,0.5]. Remove the wall-gap and r>=0 blocks from the main constraint function, but keep the 4n wall constraints for the centre-to-wall distance, because bounds alone do not enforce c-r>=0. Also precompute and cache the pair index arrays. The aim is a faster, cheaper SLSQP iteration.
backlog.title: Wall bounds instead of wall constraints

backlog.spec: Run 8 fresh starts, each with SLSQP at maxiter 60, then keep the top 3 and continue them to maxiter 200. Repeat this cycle until 40% of the time is used. Then run the existing basin hopping from the best packing. This allocates the budget by successive halving.
backlog.title: Two-pool tournament with successive halving

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, instead of jittering centres, perturb the radii: multiply each radius by exp(N(0,0.15)) and then shrink all radii by a common factor to remove overlaps. Keep the centres of the best packing and run SLSQP from there. This explores the size distribution while keeping the layout.
backlog.title: Radius-sorted rank-preserving perturbation

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, replace the common-radius SLSQP stage by 30 gradient steps. Each step is on the sum of -log(gap) barrier terms, with analytic gradients for pairs and walls, with a common radius of 0.06 and a step size that keeps all gaps positive. Then run the main SLSQP. This gives a feasible, well-spread start.
backlog.title: Log-barrier interior-point start

backlog.spec: Make MAX_ITER for fresh starts 120 in the first 20% of the time, then 200. Basin-hopping iterations use 120 if the last 3 attempts all gave sums more than 0.01 below the best, else 200. This is a simple adaptive schedule that spends fewer iterations on bad basins.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart length by remaining time

backlog.spec: Make no change to train.py (apply a trivial no-op edit such as a comment). Purpose: get another noise estimate of the incumbent so later comparisons use a true baseline.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent unchanged

backlog.spec: In the late phase, instead of jittering the best packing in place, first apply a random element of the square's symmetry group (rotation by 90 degrees multiples and reflections: swap x and y, and map x to 1-x) to the centres, then add Gaussian jitter sd 0.02 and run SLSQP. This changes only the perturbation frame and diversifies the constraint ordering seen by SLSQP, which can make SLSQP follow different paths.
backlog.title: Dihedral-symmetry restarts of best

backlog.spec: After the restart loop, take the best packing and identify active constraints (pair gaps and wall gaps below 1e-7). Solve the KKT-like square system with np.linalg.lstsq, using Newton steps on the active contact equations (d_ij = 0, wall gaps = 0) while keeping the radii as unknowns, for 5 iterations. Accept the result only if _repair gives a larger sum. Reserve 0.5 s for this step.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish of best

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, replace the objective in the main SLSQP with -sum(r^p)^(1/p) with p=0.7 for the first 60 iterations, then switch to the plain -sum(r) for the remainder. The concave power mean slightly favours equalised radii early on and gives a different basin selection. Use the analytic gradient of this objective.
backlog.title: Radius-sum objective with smooth power mean

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, with probability 0.4 pick two touching circles with different radii (centre distance within 1e-4 of r_i+r_j) and exchange their centre positions, scaling nothing else. Then run SLSQP from there with the usual jitter of sd 0.005. This is a local permutation move that keeps the contact network almost valid.
backlog.title: Swap-neighbour radii exchange in basin hopping

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, start SLSQP from the best packing with all radii multiplied by 0.7 and centres jittered by sd 0.015, so the packing is loose. SLSQP can then rearrange the contact network more freely than from a jammed state. Use it for half the basin-hopping calls.
backlog.title: Shrink-and-regrow perturbation

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, after the common-radius stage keep only pairs whose centre distance is below 0.35 in the main SLSQP, and re-check all pairs afterwards. If any pair is violated, rerun with the full set from the result. This reduces SLSQP cost per iteration (496 pairs to roughly 150), giving more restarts within the time limit.
backlog.title: Fewer pair constraints via cell list in main solve

backlog.spec: In each fresh-start iteration, build 4 random initial points, run only the cheap common-radius SLSQP stage on each, and run the full main SLSQP only on the one with the largest common radius. This is a cheap pre-selection of starts by quality, not by the loss of a full run.
backlog.title: Batch of 4 jittered starts for the best-of selection

backlog.spec: After 40% of the time, run basin hopping in cycles of 8 iterations. Within each cycle, the jitter sd decays from 0.04 to 0.005. At the start of each cycle reset the base packing to the global best. This is a sawtooth schedule that alternates exploration and exploitation.
backlog.title: Cosine time-varying jitter with periodic restarts

backlog.spec: For half of fresh starts, place about 14 circles around the square's perimeter at even spacing with a small inward offset of 0.08, and 18 circles in the interior from uniform random positions with a minimum separation of 0.12 by rejection sampling. Many good packings have a ring of boundary circles, and this biases the starts that way. Use the common-radius stage afterward.
backlog.title: Boundary-ring structured start

backlog.spec: After the restart loop, take the best packing and identify active constraints (pair gaps < 1e-7, wall gaps < 1e-7). Solve the nonlinear system of these equalities for centres and radii by Gauss-Newton/least-squares (np.linalg.lstsq with minimum-norm step), 5 iterations, using the analytic Jacobian of the active constraints. Accept only if the repaired result has a larger sum of radii. This removes the residual SLSQP tolerance error. Keep _repair as the final step.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish of best packing

backlog.spec: In the late phase, instead of jittering the best packing in place, apply a random element of the square's dihedral group (flip x, flip y, transpose, via c -> 1-c and column swaps) to the best centres first, then jitter with sd 0.02 and run SLSQP. The sum is invariant, but the random SLSQP path and the neighbour structure change. Radii are carried along unchanged.
backlog.title: Dihedral-symmetry restarts of best

backlog.spec: After each _solve_once call, fix the centres and solve the LP: maximise sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij, r_i <= wall distance, r >= 0, using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs) with sparse pair constraints for pairs with d < 0.3. Use the LP radii in place of the SLSQP radii before comparison to best, and keep the repair as a safety net. This gives exact radii for the centres and makes the ranking of candidates more faithful.
backlog.title: LP-optimal radii after every SLSQP

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, first solve a 28-circle problem with the cheap common-radius SLSQP and then the main SLSQP with maxiter 60. Then add 4 circles at the centres of the largest empty holes. Find the holes by sampling 2000 random points and taking the points with the largest clearance, spreading them out. Give the new circles radius 0.02 and run the full main SLSQP on all 32. This builds on a structured, relaxed packing.
backlog.title: Smaller-circle count continuation

backlog.spec: In the main SLSQP for fresh starts, optimise the objective -(mean(r^p))^(1/p)*n, with p=0.5 for the first 60 iterations (it favours equal-sized circles), then p=1 (the true sum) for the remaining iterations, warm-started from the previous result. The aim is to reach different basins than a direct sum objective. Use only the true sum for comparing candidates.
backlog.title: Power-mean objective continuation

backlog.spec: In the late phase, build a child packing by taking the circles of the best packing with x<0.5 and the circles with x>=0.5 from the second-best distinct packing (keep a pool of the top 2). If the count is not 32, drop the smallest circles, or add circles at random holes with radius 0.03. Jitter by 0.01 and run SLSQP. This is a crossover that combines half-packings.
backlog.title: Reflected-best crossover

backlog.spec: For half of fresh starts, make initial centres with a simple Lubachevsky-Stillinger-style procedure. Give 32 random points random velocities. Grow the common radius from 0.02 in steps of 0.002 and resolve overlaps by pushing apart overlapping pairs along their line of centres, for 200 vectorised numpy sweeps with wall clamping. Then run the main SLSQP from those centres with radii set to the achieved radius. Use the achieved radius instead of the common-radius SLSQP stage.
backlog.title: Event-driven billiards compression start

backlog.spec: In the late phase, produce 64 jittered copies of the best packing at once and relax each with 30 vectorised numpy gradient steps on the penalty sum(max(0, r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2) plus wall violations, with radii fixed at their current values scaled by 0.98. Pick the 3 copies with the smallest penalty and run full SLSQP only on those. This uses cheap screening to choose which perturbations to spend SLSQP time on.
backlog.title: Cheap-evaluation parallel batch of perturbations via vectorised penalty

backlog.spec: In the late phase, perturb the best packing, then run SLSQP on only the variables of a random local cluster (a random circle plus its 8 nearest neighbours). The other circles are frozen, and constraints between the cluster and frozen circles are kept. This has about 27 variables, so each solve is far cheaper, which allows many more local moves. Then run one full SLSQP with maxiter 60 when the local result improves the sum.
backlog.title: Reduced-variable SLSQP with fixed small circles

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 0.4 switch with an adaptive rule. Keep a running log of fresh-start results. Switch to basin hopping when the best fresh result was found more than 30% of the elapsed time ago, or at 0.55 of the time limit at the latest. In the basin-hopping phase, return to fresh starts for one run after 8 consecutive failures to improve. Do not use a stagnation count of restarts alone (slot 33 did that). This version uses elapsed-time-since-best.
backlog.title: Adaptive time split by improvement rate

backlog.spec: In fresh starts, run the main SLSQP in 3 stages with objective -sum(r) + lam*sum((r-mean(r))^2), with lam = 0.5, 0.15, 0, each stage warm-started from the previous one with maxiter about 70. The final stage must be the true objective. Use this for half of fresh starts.
backlog.title: Soft-min spread regulariser decaying to zero

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, with probability 0.3 pick a random vertical or horizontal line. Shift all circles on one side by a random offset of up to 0.05 perpendicular to the line, clip the centres, shrink the radii by 20%, and run SLSQP. Otherwise use the normal jitter.
backlog.title: Large-perturbation row shift with a cut and shuffle

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, run SLSQP on the sum of r^p with p=0.5 for 40 iterations (it favours equal radii), then p=1. The total iteration count stays the same as now. The common-radius init stays as the first stage.
backlog.title: Radius-inflation continuation

backlog.spec: Write a numpy function that runs 64 random starts at once as an (B,n,2) array. It does 200 steps of gradient descent with momentum on a penalty energy: overlap^2 plus wall violation^2, minus the radius sum, with the radii as variables. Take the best 3 by penalised score and polish them with the existing SLSQP. Use this for the first 15% of the time to seed the best packing.
backlog.title: Batch-evaluated vectorised penalty relaxation

backlog.spec: In the late phase, take the best packing and sort the radii. Perturb by adding noise to the radii of the 6 smallest circles (sd 0.02) and moving their centres to random points in the largest empty space. Pick the space by sampling 300 points and taking the one furthest from every circle edge. Then run SLSQP at maxiter 200. This differs from the earlier reinsert moves because the radii get a fresh start and the 6 circles move together.
backlog.title: Two-size-class constrained basin hop

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, build the pair list from the perturbed centres with a cutoff on gap < 0.08 instead of 0.15. Then run SLSQP. After the run, check for violated pruned pairs. If any exist, add them and re-run for 30 iterations. This should give more basin-hopping steps per second.
backlog.title: Cheaper SLSQP via active pair pruning in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Take the best packing and its contact graph. Perturb the centres with sd 0.015. Then alternate 5 times: solve an LP for the radii (maximise sum r with linearised distance constraints about the current centres and a trust region of 0.02 on the centre moves). Use scipy linprog with highs, with variables dx, dy, r. Then run SLSQP from the result. This is a sequential LP step that gives a better start than plain jitter.
backlog.title: Fixed-topology LP seeding from the best packing

incumbent.description: For fresh random starts, first run a cheap SLSQP maximizing a single common radius (about 50 iterations), then use those spread centres with equal radii as the start for the full free-radius SLSQP.

memo:
Helped: only search-strategy changes. Slot 4 (basin hopping from jittered copies of the best packing after 40% of the time) gave -0.0050 over 2 runs. Slot 7 (cheap common-radius SLSQP init for fresh starts) gave -0.0063 over 2 runs. The incumbent is -2.9366 over 2 runs, about 0.0004 below the published 2.9370, so little headroom is left.

Did not help: constraint reformulation (+0.0140), analytic Jacobians (+0.0007), final polish (+0.0049), mirror starts (+0.0014), L-BFGS-B penalty init (+0.0056), per-circle random radii (+0.0081), log-barrier init (+0.0112). Most later single-run tweaks sit within noise (sd about 0.0034). Many slots scored exactly -2.9374, so the same optimum seems to be found each time.

Next: replicate the incumbent once. Replicate slots 14, 25 and 10 only if budget allows. Don't repeat tried ideas. Further gains are probably below the noise, so consider stopping.
